subject: Post-call: prompt collection & model-fit next steps (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: prompt collection & model-fit next steps (Acme)

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet you and Priya. Quick recap + next steps so we stay aligned:

- Goal: get a representative prompt set from Acme so we can run model-fit evals and share quantifiable lift / regressions for your use cases (product descriptions + returns summarization).
- Deliverables (from Redwood): recommended models + perf/cost benchmarks, an initial eval run on your prompts, redaction guidance for PII, and a prioritized list of edge cases.

What we need from you:
1) A CSV with ~200 representative prompts (real user examples + a few synthetic edge cases). Include a column for expected output style (tone/length).
2) A short list of known failure modes / edge cases (e.g., messy OCR, truncated receipts, multi-language).
3) Your redaction policy: do you want us to redact PII before sending to Redwood’s hosted evals, or do you prefer to run evals on-prem / in your VPC?

Attached is a starter template (acme_prompts_v1.csv) and our redaction guidance (redaction_guidance_v1.pdf). I’ve also linked the benchmark page we’ll use as a baseline.

Next steps: if you can share the CSV by EOD Friday (Aug 28) we’ll queue an initial run and aim to return results within 3 business days. If that works, I’ll schedule a 30m sync for Tues to review results.

Thanks — happy to take questions.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0186

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: prompt collection & model-fit next steps (Acme)

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A couple quick clarifications before we compile the CSV:

- Sample prompts: we have a column of user queries and another with product context. Is it OK to include both in the same row, or do you prefer two separate columns?
- Redaction: our security team is conservative. We’d prefer that any PII be redacted client-side before upload. Is there an easy redaction checklist you recommend?

Example prompts (paste):
1) "What is the return window for order #12345?" (expect: short policy snippet + link)
2) "My receipt shows two charges for the same item — what happened?" (expect: empathetic apology + next steps)
3) "\u000546\u0004c1\u00063f\u00e8\u00bd\u00a4\u00ef\u00bc\u008c\u00e4\u00b8\u00ad\u00e6\u0096\u0087\u00ef\u00bc\u0084\u00e6\u0088\u0090\u00e4\u00b8\u009a\u00ef\u00bc\u0089" (Chinese prompt — expect: short bullet with size info)

We can assemble ~250 examples and flag about 30 known edge cases. Can you confirm the CSV template and the expected columns? Also, if we redact on our side, what fields are ok to strip and still preserve evaluation fidelity?

On redaction policy: Priya (cc) is our security lead — she’ll weigh in on whether we can share PII for evaluation or need an on-prem run.

—
Alex Chen
Head of Product 
Acme Retail
alex.chen@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: prompt collection & model-fit next steps (Acme)

Perfect — thanks Alex. Quick answers and guidance below. I’ll include the starter template again as an attachment.

- CSV columns: please use these columns (we included in acme_prompts_v1.csv): 
  * prompt_id (unique)
  * user_query (the raw user text)
  * product_context (optional structured context you pass to the model)
  * expected_output (short description of what a correct response looks like)
  * language (en/zh/etc)
  * edge_case_flag (yes/no)

Keeping user_query + product_context in separate columns is strongly preferred — it gives us flexibility to test context-injection vs context-free prompts.

- Redaction checklist: we recommend client-side redaction for any direct identifiers (full credit card numbers, government IDs, full SSNs). For evaluation fidelity, keep format markers (e.g., "<ORDER_ID>") and include an anonymized token so we preserve structure. Our attached redaction_guidance_v1.pdf has examples. If you prefer Redwood to run the evals in your VPC, we can do that under an enterprise trial (we’d need a short MOU).

- Model recommendations (high-level):
  * For short QA and policy retrieval: try Redwood-2.1-medium (cost-friendly) and Redwood-3.7-prod for higher-quality, latency-tolerant flows.
  * For multilingual and noisy text (OCR receipts): run a side eval on a robust open checkpoint we call "mpt-7b-multilang" (we’ll surface tradeoffs).

Benchmark link: https://redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/acme-nli — that page shows token-cost, latency p50/p95, and a small eval snapshot for these models. I attached a static HTML export (redwood_benchmarks_acme_nli.html).

Edge-case guidance: please flag examples with truncated context, embedded OCR artifacts, and mixed-language sentences. We’ll mark those in the eval and surface per-case failure modes.

Next steps (confirming):
- You: share CSV (~200–300 rows) + edge case list by Fri (Aug 28) — client-side redaction ok.
- Us: run initial eval, return a dashboard + top 10 failure cases within 3 business days.
- Sync: Tue Sep 1 (I’ll propose 30m) to review results and rollout plan.

If Priya needs an NDA addendum or wants an on-prem run, cc Vivek and we’ll pull the security/infra team into the conversation.

Thanks again — looking forward to the prompts.



—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0186

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: prompt collection & model-fit next steps (Acme)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of quick notes from security:

- We will redact direct identifiers client-side (order numbers can be replaced with <ORDER_ID>, emails with <EMAIL>). That should be sufficient for initial evals.
- We’d like to see the eval run metadata removed from any public-run logs (no user tokens in traces). Can Redwood confirm logs are scrubbed for hosted evals?

Alex and I will upload the CSV later today — expect ~240 rows with language tags and edge_case_flag populated. If any of those rows are sensitive, we’ll mark them and request an on-prem run for that subset.

Priya
Security Lead, Acme Retail
priya.shah@acme.com
